1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.strategy: Forces the bishop to decide. If Black takes on c3, White accepts doubled pawns for the bishop pair and aims to cure the weakness by exchanging on d5 and to build the centre with the bishop pair behind it.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence: Normal Variation, Sämisch Deferred

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.strategy: Breaks the pin, so ...Bxc3 no longer doubles the pawns. The price is a tempo and a passive dark-squared bishop on d2, which leaves Black free to put pressure on the c4 pawn and the centre.
Develops with pressure on d4 now that the pin is lifted and ...Bxc3 would not double any pawns. Black plays for piece activity and a central break, with the c4 pawn as a target.
